land.text: the Provinces of Cumana, Guayana and Maracaibo, and the Islands of Margarita and Trinidad, with Caracas

predecessors.note: The Royal Decree of 8 September 1777 'separated the Provinces of Cumana, Guayana and Maracaibo, and Islands of Margarita and Trinidad' from New Granada and added them to the Captaincy General of Venezuela.

land.text: Venezuela as part of Gran Colombia

successors.note: 'Independence for Venezuela was consolidated in 1821 as part of Gran Colombia'; after 'the collapse of Gran Colombia in 1830' the provinces 'constituted the territory of the new independent republic of Venezuela' (Cliopatria 'Venezuela' from 1834). The infobox gives 'Capitulation: 24 July 1823'; Puerto Cabello held out to October or November 1823.

capitals.name: Caracas
capitals.note: Infobox capital Santiago de Leon de Caracas; the royalist seat after 1812 was Caracas and, after 1821, Puerto Cabello/Coro in practice (page silent).

keyframe_review.note: The captaincy at creation (8 September 1777): Caracas, Cumana, Guayana, Maracaibo, Margarita and Trinidad. No area on the page; the shape is Cliopatria's Spanish Empire of 1777 inside Venezuela, plus a 70 km disc for Trinidad. The Guayana claim reaches the Essequibo, which the page does not draw.
'Control of the Province of Trinidad was lost to the British in 1797.' The 1786 Audiencia of Caracas changed justice, not borders.

minus.text: the provinces that declared independence, as Cliopatria draws the First Republic

correction.text: the royalist provinces: Coro, Maracaibo and Guayana, and what the junta did not hold

keyframe_review.note: After the Caracas junta of 19 April 1810 'Maracaibo Province, and Guayana Province, and one district, Coro, never recognized the Caracas Junta': drawn as Venezuela minus Cliopatria's First Republic shape (400,000 km2, the seven of ten provinces).
After Miranda's capitulation of 25 July 1812 the republic is gone: Monteverde holds all Venezuela.

minus.text: the Second Republic of 1813-1814, as Cliopatria draws it

correction.text: Venezuela without the republican Caracas and centre

keyframe_review.note: From Bolivar's entry into Caracas on 6 August 1813 the republican zone returns (Second Republic); Mariño held the east from Cumana. Cliopatria draws the Republic of Venezuela only for 1811 and 1814 (400,000 km2 both times): its 1814 shape is used for 1813.

'Mariño and Bolivar joined their forces, but they were defeated by Boves in 1814'; in 1815 Morillo's expedition retook the north, leaving the patriots only the southern plains and, from 1816, Guayana: the royalists hold the whole of Venezuela through 1816.

minus.text: Angostura/Guayana and the plains held by the patriots

correction.text: Venezuela without the patriot Guayana and llanos

keyframe_review.note: 1817: 'Piar and Marino had occupied defenceless Angostura' and Bolivar took over there; the llanos stayed with Paez. The page does not draw the frontier, so the patriot zone is the state of Bolivar plus the Venezuelan llanos.

correction.text: Venezuela without the patriot south and Barinas

keyframe_review.note: 'Paez occupied Barinas and, from New Granada, Bolivar invaded Venezuela' (1819); Angostura proclaimed the Republic of Colombia on 17 December 1819.

correction.text: Coro, Maracaibo and Puerto Cabello, the last royalist ground

keyframe_review.note: After Carabobo (1821) 'Cumana fell shortly thereafter'; the royalists keep 'Coro and Maracaibo from 1810' and Puerto Cabello 'until 1823'. The Spanish fleet lost the Battle of Lake Maracaibo in 1823 and Puerto Cabello capitulated in October or November 1823 (the page is inconsistent).

region.text: Cumana, Guayana, Maracaibo, Margarita and Trinidad with Caracas

ledger.note: 1777 (8 September): the Captaincy General of Venezuela is created. 'Created on September 8, 1777, through the Royal Decree of Graces of 1777', joining Cumana, Guayana, Maracaibo, Margarita and Trinidad to the Intendancy of Caracas (created in 1776).
1797: Britain takes Trinidad. 'Control of the Province of Trinidad was lost to the British in 1797.' The page names neither the month nor the war.

region.text: the provinces that declared independence, as Cliopatria draws the First Republic

ledger.note: 1810 (19 April): the Caracas council deposes the governor. 'On April 19, 1810 the municipal council of Caracas headed a successful movement to depose the Spanish Governor'; independence was declared on 5 July 1811 by seven of ten provinces. The zone is Cliopatria's First Republic shape.

region.text: the provinces that declared independence, as Cliopatria draws the First Republic

ledger.note: 1812 (25 July): Miranda capitulates. 'Miranda capitulated to Monteverde and signed an armistice on 25 July 1812', ending the First Republic.

region.text: the Second Republic of 1813-1814, as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 1813 (6 August): Bolivar enters Caracas. 'Bolivar entered Caracas on 6 August 1813, proclaiming the restoration of the Venezuelan Republic'; Marino held the east from Cumana.

region.text: the Second Republic of 1813-1814, as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 1814: Boves destroys the Second Republic. 'Mariño and Bolivar joined their forces, but they were defeated by Boves in 1814'; the republicans evacuated Caracas for the east and Piar held out at Carupano.

union.text: Angostura and the province of Guayana

ledger.note: 1817: the patriots take Angostura and Guayana. 'Piar and Marino had occupied defenceless Angostura' in 1817 and Bolivar took over there; Piar and MacGregor defeated Morales at El Juncal in September 1816 and moved south. The llanos stayed with Paez.

1819: Barinas falls. 'Paez occupied Barinas and, from New Granada, Bolivar invaded Venezuela' after Boyaca (August 1819); the Congress of Angostura proclaimed the Republic of Colombia on 17 December 1819.

minus.text: Coro, Maracaibo and Puerto Cabello, the last royalist ground

region.text: Venezuela except Coro, Maracaibo and Puerto Cabello

ledger.note: 1821: Carabobo breaks the royalist hold. 'In 1821, the Gran Colombian army won a decisive victory at the second Battle of Carabobo'; Cumana 'fell shortly thereafter'. Coro, Maracaibo and Puerto Cabello are what the royalists keep.

region.text: Coro, Maracaibo and Puerto Cabello, the last royalist ground

ledger.note: 1823 (24 July): the last royalist force surrenders. The infobox gives 'Capitulation: 24 July 1823'; the Spanish fleet was beaten at Lake Maracaibo and Puerto Cabello 'finally capitulat[ed] in October 1823' (the page's belligerent list says November).

notes:
Written by am-06-x from two pages (budget 2-5). Not settled:
(1) No area on any page; shapes are Cliopatria's Spanish Empire inside Venezuela, with patriot zones taken from Cliopatria's Republic of Venezuela rows (1811 and 1814, 400,000 km2, no 1812-1813 shape) or from region names. The royalist holdouts of 1821-1823 are the states of Falcon (Coro), Zulia (Maracaibo) and a disc around Puerto Cabello, the researcher's reading of 'Coro and Maracaibo from 1810; Puerto Cabello until 1823'.
(2) The captaincy page's Guayana is the whole Orinoco-Essequibo country; its western Essequibo claim (now Guyana) is not drawn. The 1786 Audiencia of Caracas changed jurisdiction only. New Granada's own dossier lists Venezuelan provinces under both 1777 and 1786-1810: the infobox date 8 September 1777 is used.
(3) The end date: infobox 'Capitulation: 24 July 1823'; Puerto Cabello held out to October (text) or November 1823 (belligerent list). The dossier ends 1823-07.
(4) The Second Republic and the Third Republic (Angostura 1817-1819) have no Cliopatria rows after 1814 (the republic is a Cliopatria row only for 1811 and 1814): a gap-filler may want a rebel dossier for them. Counterpart republic-of-venezuela stands for the patriot republics throughout.
